correctness.rationale: For m>=2 there is no universal vertex and all cross-part edges form adjacent dominating pairs, giving gamma_tR=4. On any isolate-free graph of order>=5 with no universal vertex, weight-four total Roman labellings exist iff an adjacent dominating pair exists. The listed 4-deletion witness at m=2 and 5-deletion witness for all m>=3 remove all such pairs without creating isolates. Independently enumerated every edge deletion of size <=3 for m=2 and <=4 for m=3,4; among the 299,2514,6192 isolate-free deletion sets respectively, all retained a dominating edge. For m>4 at most four C-vertices meet deletions, so an induced four-representative K_{2,2,4} preserves all deletions and has no isolate; its remaining dominating edge also dominates untouched C. This proves universal lower bound five. m=1 universal vertex requires exactly one deletion. The actual verify.py finite certificate code was read and independent enum matched its domain; computed finite certificates plus the infinite reduction, not a timeout.
residual_risks: Finite m=2,3,4 obstruction counts are exact only because all deletion combinations were enumerated; unbounded m rests on the separate induction/restriction argument.
